OK. I have now seen that some of my descriptions are alien to many - this is because I did not have the available "incarnation time" to wade through the amount of chaff at Forex Factory or Baby Pips to find the wheat. But still, by luck, and a lot of good fortune, found my own way through the ocean or sharks that circle our trading business and come out relatively unscathed the other side.

Most terms are learned from others - a few are my own - All my examples are from a trading SHORT perspective - I don't want to type examples needlessly twice

MOMO - a series of candles that together form a big candle in my minds eye - This is the "MOMENTUM " that has the POWER to break a POINTY PLACE (it is not to be confused with a long candle formed by a liquidity gap in the middle of nowhere)

Lets be clear - If momo doesn't break a Pointy Place - It aint MOMO

POINTY PLACE - Posts 29 through 31 save my typing fingers

SHELF - same as above but a different shape - ( so shelfey rather than pointy) - I personally usually stick with just saying Pointy Place - its all part of my charm!

A HOOK - what better term for a pirate - imagine a RBD (Rally Base Drop) - a lovely new targetable supply is often found when the DBD (Drop Base Drop) under that forms a "hook" or if you prefer a "rose thorn" - supply can sometimes be at the top of that;

ZERO LINE This is where traders take a trade, they all see it together and join in a short - they this sit on the trade as they go into profit - price then surprisingly reverses! When price returns to their entry area the feel fear of loss - so wherever they had there stop loss - they move the stops to their entry point - those orders (their profit) are now all in the same place - the market makers can now target the rich pickings all in the same place and buy the original traders good positions off them at a discount - price then carries on down - to the howls of anguish coming from the traders who moved their stops only to see price rush off in there original direction - what fun!

SPACE - my preferred - and imho - The Very Best Money Management System Ever-and I will take some convincing to prove otherwise - if you have the slightest abilty whatsoever you can really do some damage with space - and, for a special treat for all of you here, I might even draw a cool diagram - if I find time.

Why use space for your Money Management? - Well, space acts to protect you against inevitable mistakes - space takes the importance of "winning" out of the equation and at the same time allows you to become aggressive with your held profit to make a killing -for some reason it takes some time to "get it"- but once you do you'll never go back.

As regards using the fib tool overlaid on your space "box" - The fib tool lets you know WHEN you can be aggressive with your space.

You NEVER allow your space to be destroyed with one (or even a run of bad trades) -my mentor has not managed to burn through his space in three years! - and yes he makes many mistakes - this WORKS

FAT CAT - Imagine a cat - happily bouncing away on a trampoline and tapping his head on the ceiling from time to time -

Then he finally gets up enough steam to "really go for it" so he slams up through the ceiling - He is curious about who lives upstairs

Only as soon as he can see into to upstairs room he's so curious about - the owner greets him with an effin great cricket bat, slaps him on the top of his head and sends him straight back where he came from.

The supply demand story for the "fat cat" is the change of supply to demand where price breaks through the ceiling - the cricket bat is BIG supply that send him packing and on the way down the demand he caused on the way up is "broken" and HAS to become supply again at THAT point - after his adventure into the upstairs apartment the cat reaches the trampoline with his head on the sore side - where do you think he will have a good chance bouncing off next time he goes up

To me it is a simple as it says - it is a rejection of price (on any timeframe (but the higher timframe the better))

OK thinking about it - it is price breaking a Supply or Demand level - just work backwards from there - there is a place somewhere before the break of the pointy place that price left you a sign - it is the place where the bloody big order was put on by a bank - it is maybe hidden, within one of the timeframes. - I am very new here but I think you guys call it a Decision Point DP?

i am working out how to explain "space" atm - I do not use MO's fractional notation - it confuses me - I imagin "space" in my head as a "bucket of money" - with the bucket as tall as i want it to be - the taller the bucket - the less concentrated your cash - a short bucket would have your cash - and therefore your lot size much higher.

you NEVER burn through your space - If it gets chisled away by some losses - you reduce your position size.

Space is a form of trading that involves delayed gratification - you split your account into two -

The big "leverage" side of the ledger, this dictates your maximum lot size - this part of your account is protected and SAFE

The "risk" side of the ledger (the bucket) is to be used agressively - you do NOT put your profit into the main "leverage" side of your account (this rule HAS to be broken on occasion)

The profit is stuffed into your "bucket" - therefore driving up your lot size - this results in so much faster an account growth than the conventional "add your win to your account, and lets see what new tiny lot size increase we have made"

YOU decide when you want to reset your account - ie when you have reached a desired percentage growth. Typically you can cut out 2 to 4 percent of your account as your risk. IMPORTANT - you NEVER use all your risk on a single trade ( imagine nursmaiding a small account within your account)

So - just what are my choices?

Well - because I started this trade sequence with 240 pips of space:

In effect I can trade the 1162 pips of gained SPACE for a larger lot size (this is what I do)

Therefore reducing my SPACE to 581 pips would double my lot size - for no extra risk

Reducing SPACE from 1162 to 290 pips would quadruple my lot size - for no extra risk I started the move with 240 pips of space so even if I quadrupled my original lot size, I would still be have the same risk!

Yet another possibility is stripping out my original risk - then I can get aggressive with the markets money and not my own

Remember I can reduce lot size and gain more space - or get aggressive and reduce space for a higher lot size

In other words I can trade my space - i do not wait until now to do this - I am "pumping" my space during the whole of the trade sequence

If I could summaries my trading education/path. Not in any order of importance.

1. Quality information - Sam Seiden Vid's and Articles (for me). Stay focused I have strayed myself as I love learning but it can be a distraction.

2. Training - Go over old charts find pointy places and ask why did price turn there? Draw a line and change time frames. Be a detective. Take screen shots build up a library. With time you will notice some patterns then you will notice how patterns work together.

Investigate the different elements of a setup, for example study how price approaches a RBD and the effect. Investigate the different elements. If's homework's are spot on here in my opinion. Chris Lori Is also strong here he was an Olympic athlete in one of the toughest sports and he approaches trading in the same way - training for the main event (Essential Qualities of Successful FX Traders Video Series).

3. Build some trading muscle - Expose yourself to the market. Get used to the emotions. Hold trades for a day, 2 days. Wait a week for a setup. Don't look at the screen let your trades run etc. Again a type of exercise for the main event. Read Trading in the zone, trade cold.

4. Money Management - is an art in itself. Phantom of the pits rules 1 and 2. Info on poker players etc etc, will give you ideas. Fxstreet have some good education material on money management.

The recipe for success in anything is pretty much the same. Hard word, dedication, belief in yourself.

The education may take a while so priority one should be to keep yourself in the game whilst you learn:-

1. Demo. --Time--2. Live very low risk. --Time--3. Spank the market.

If you loose your bank role you can't play at the table and learn.

Cheers,

I see youre trying to quantify by what you see, in a measurement perspective.

Understand what length means in the context of S/D trading.

RBD example

the left 'leg' - price has found demand/buyers, and price rises/rallies

the base/top - price has found equilibrium for a relative period of time, but inevitably succumbs to sellers and falls/drops

the right 'leg' - sellers are dropping price, how far depends on price finding a demand that can overcome the sellers.

Now that you are thinking about the ACTUAL MARKET DYNAMICS and not just measuring a leg; if the right leg is in fact longer than the left leg that means the demand that started the whole RBD has been broken and the sellers that dropped that turned price must be pretty powerful. MOMO has been quantified.

SO YES HARSHTHAKR AN RBD WITH A RIGHT LEG LARGER THAN THE LEFT IS SIGNIFICANT AND POWERFUL BUT ALWAYS IN THE CONTEXT OF THE BIG PICTURE.
